EMERGENCY LANDING PROCEDURES
In the unlikely event that an emergency landing should become necessary,
listen carefully to all instructions given by the crew.
BRACING POSITION
If the order is given to assume the bracing position,
you should do the following:
• Loosen your necktie and collar
• Remove your glasses and dentures
• Remove all sharp objects from your pockets
• Fasten your seat belt securely
• Adopt the braced position as illustrated
SPECIAL INFORMATION FOR OVERWATER FLIGHTS
Should an overwater emergency landing (ditching) become necessary, you should
be aware of certain special procedures:
• There will be two impacts, one when the tail section touches the
water, and another when the wings and main body of the
aircraft touch down
• After the second impact, unfasten your seat belt and make an
orderly evacuation from the aircraft
• You should inflate your life jacket only AFTER you are outside
of the aircraft
LIFE JACKETS AND FLOTATION SEAT CUSHIONS
A placard on the seat in front of you will tell if this aircraft is equipped with LIFE
JACKETS or FLOTATION SEAT CUSHIONS. You should become familiar with the
use of whichever is aboard this aircraft by reading the applicable instructions below:
HOW TO USE A LIFE JACKET
• Remove the Life Jacket from under your seat
• Hold the Life Jacket with the lamp to the front
• Push your head through the neck opening
• Insert waist strap through buckle and pull tight
• Inflate by pulling down sharply on the plastic knob only AFTER
you are outside the aircraft
• If necessary, the Life Jacket may be inflated by blowing into
the mouthpiece provided
• The light may be activated by pulling the plug from the bottom
of the battery. When the sea water contacts the battery, the
light automatically comes on
HOW TO USE A FLOTATION SEAT CUSHION
• Remove the bottom seat cushion from your seat
• Hold the seat cushion directly in front of you
• Place your arms through the loops like putting on a coat backwards
• Lock your hands in front of you to hold cushion to chest
• Do not wear cushion on your back as this will cause you to float
face down
PLEASE DO NOT REMOVE THIS CARD FROM THE AIRCRAFT

MISSIONARY FLIGHTS INTERNATIONAL
IMPORTANT INFORMATION
Your crew welcomes you aboard MISSIONARY FLIGHTS INTERNATIONAL. You
are flying aboard a Douglas DC-3 Airliner, the world's finest and most respected
transport aircraft. Your Captain has met the skill and experience requirements
established by the U.S. Government for all airline pilots, as well as specific profi-
ciency standards in the operation of a Douglas DC-3.
Every effort has been made to eliminate the chance of an emergency situation.
We do ask, however, that you take a moment to study this card to become
familiar with this aircraft for your comfort and safety.
SEAT BELTS
During all takeoffs and landings, your
seat belt should be securely fasten-
ed. The SEAT BELT signs will advise
you when you should fasten your
seat belt. We do recommend that you
leave your seat belt on at all times
while seated. Seat backs are to be in
the upright position during takeoffs
SMOKING IS PRO-
HIBITED AT ALL TIMES ON MFI AIR.
CRAFT.
EMERGENCY EXITS
Three emergency exits are available
to the passengers on our DC-3 - two
window exits on either side of the
cabin at the rear of the wing and the
main
cabin
airstair door
through
which you entered. We ask that you
not tamper with them unless an
emergency situation exists.
LAVATORY
The restroom door is on the left as
you face the rear of the aircraft. USE
ONLY THIS DOOR! Remain clear of
all other doors.
AIRCRAFT GALLEY
Refreshments are available from the
MFI galley. DO NOT attempt to use
the galley yourself.
Please ask a
crew member to serve you.
HELP KEEP IT CLEAN
The crew is responsible for cleaning
this aircraft after each flight.
You
can help by giving all trash to the
flight attendant for disposal.
NOT place gum in ash trays or under
seats. DO NOT use airsickness bags
for trash disposal.
The diagram below shows the location of the emergency exits on this aircraft.
